subject: Post-demo: Lumina performance targets & customer-led stress window coordination
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Lumina performance targets & next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Targets we agreed to qualify: P95 latency <= 150ms for text-generation (streaming enabled), sustained throughput of 750 tokens/s, and support for 200 concurrent connections during peak sampling windows.
- Customer-led stress window: Lumina to run a controlled stress run against our staging endpoint using k6 (you mentioned existing scripts).
- Redwood to provide: test accounts, IP allowlist ranges, a short test plan (what to watch for), and a fallback model variant if quantized runtime diverges.

Can you confirm the preferred test window(s) — we suggested Oct 20–22, 0100–0500 PT — and share the k6 script or repo link. Marissa, looping you in to prepare the staging artifacts and test accounts. Tessa, would you own IP allowlist and runbook notes?

Thanks — I’ll draft an ops checklist once windows are confirmed.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@luminahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Mehta <rahul.mehta@luminahealth.com>, Lumina SRE Team <sre@luminahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Lumina performance targets & next steps

Thanks Rishi — succinct summary, much appreciated. Confirming:

- SLOs are correct from our side (P95 <=150ms streaming, throughput 750 tokens/s, concurrency 200).
- Preferred initial stress window: Oct 21, 0200–0600 PT (narrower window so we can bring systems back quickly).
- We will run customer-controlled k6 load from our CI runners (Ubuntu VMs) and can share the script.

Action items for Redwood: please provide staging endpoints, test credentials, and the IP ranges we need to allowlist. We will attach the k6 script and a short runbook once we finish a quick linting pass.

Aisha Khan
Senior Product Manager, Lumina Health
aisha.k@luminahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@luminahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 07:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Staging artifacts and test accounts for Lumina stress run

Hi Aisha — prepping the staging side now. Inventory below and what I’m attaching: 

Attachments: lumina_k6_script_v1.js (k6 script stub), lumina_test_accounts.csv (one-time API keys), redwood_test_instructions.pdf (short runbook).

Staging endpoints:
- generation (streaming): https://staging-redwood.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
- fallback model variant (lower-precision): https://staging-redwood.redwood.ai/v1/generate/fast
\Credentials:
- Test API key: RL-TEST-LUM-0001 (in lumina_test_accounts.csv) — scoped to staging only and rate limited to the test window.

Notes on the k6 script: it exercises streaming chunking by opening 200 concurrent virtual users and ramping to 750 tokens/s aggregate; you’ll see markers for latency capture and a final summary metric we emit as x-redwood-p95. If you want modifications to concurrency pattern or a longer soak, tell us the exact change and we’ll update.

Tessa — IP allowlist ranges from Lumina? Once we have those we’ll provision ACLs for the staging cluster.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@luminahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staging artifacts and test accounts for Lumina stress run

Thanks — I’ve queued the ACL change. Aisha, can you confirm the public egress IPs for your k6 runners? We need CIDR blocks to open on the staging load-balancer.

Quick reminder about test etiquette: during the window we’ll expose a short debug metric endpoint (/health/debug) that returns per-node queue depth — please don’t poll it more than once per minute to avoid poll noise.

I’ll also publish a short checklist in Drive (link below) with the rollback steps and how to toggle to the fallback model.

-Tessa
Platform Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@luminahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staging artifacts and test accounts for Lumina stress run

Quick update from our SRE: confirmed egress IP ranges below and attaching cleaned k6 script.

Egress IPs (CIDR):
- 35.182.120.0/24
- 34.102.55.128/25

We will run Oct 21, 0200–0600 PT as discussed. The attached k6 script is lumina_k6_script_v1.js (we removed local debug hooks). We expect a short smoke at 02:00 then a 3-hour ramp/steady phase. If anything unexpected happens we’ll stop and notify the thread; otherwise we’ll upload k6 cloud summary to the HubSpot link.

Attachments: lumina_k6_script_v1.js

Thanks everyone — looking forward to validating the streaming SLOs.

Aisha
